Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. Tanzid Hasan and Parvez Hossain Emon walk out as the opening pair for Bangladesh with Fareed Ahmad ready to bowl the first over for Afghanistan.
... The Run Chase ...

Rahmanullah Gurbaz expressed satisfaction with his team's performance, despite not batting exactly how he wanted to. He credited his captain and coach for trusting him with significant responsibility, batting at number 3, a position he's not accustomed to but appreciated the faith shown in him. Gurbaz hopes to build on this momentum in future games. When defending their total, he assured that the team would give its best effort.

Bangladesh's bowling was impressive overall, although Taskin Ahmed and Tanzim Hasan Sakib were expensive in parts of the innings despite picking up crucial wickets. Nasum Ahmed and Mustafizur Rahman bowled tightly during the Powerplay and middle overs, respectively, and took important wickets to restrict Afghanistan's scoring.

Afghanistan's innings struggled initially, with regular wickets falling. Rahmanullah Gurbaz, batting out of position at number 3, provided stability with a 40-run knock. Mohammad Nabi's crucial cameo of 38 runs at a quick pace was instrumental in helping Afghanistan post over 150. Sharafuddin Ashraf also contributed with a late-innings cameo of 17 runs, adding some valuable runs to the total.
Afghanistan staged a recovery, posting a total of over 150 after being reduced to 40/4 in the 7th over.

OUT! RUN OUT! On a length around middle and off, Sharafuddin Ashraf smashes this to wide long on for a single. Noor Ahmad comes for the second willing to sacrifice for the team and ends up doing so. Noor Ahmad tried to sneak another quick single with Ashraf, but the throw from the fielder went to Sakib at the bowler's end, who then threw it to the keeper, Jaker Ali, who removed the bails, resulting in Noor Ahmad's run-out. Afghanistan's innings ends at 151/9.

Commentary.Commentary: All set to begin! The two sides stride out in the middle and line up for their respective national anthem. It will be Bangladesh's first, followed by the national anthem of Afghanistan. We are now done with the pre-match formalities. Bangladesh fielders now take their respective field positions. Ibrahim Zadran and Sediqullah Atal will open up for Afghanistan. Taskin Ahmed has the new ball in hand. Let's go...

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Sediqullah Atal, Darwish Rasooli, Azmatullah Omarzai, Rashid Khan (C), Mohammad Nabi, Sharafuddin Ashraf, Noor Ahmad, Mohammad Ishaq, Fareed Ahmad.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Jaker Ali (C)(WK), Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon, Saif Hassan, Nurul Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Rishad Hossain, Nasum Ahmed, Tanzim Hasan Sakib.
TOSS - Afghanistan have won the toss and will BAT first.

Considering the venue, Sharjah's historically spinning wickets strongly favor Afghanistan's world-class trio of spinners. Coupled with the absence of Litton Das and the recent batting struggles of Bangladesh, Afghanistan holds a notable advantage. So, which side will come out on top? We shall find out. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Bangladesh, meanwhile, is dealing with the absence of their regular captain, Litton Das, pushing them to rely on the experience of others. While the fast-bowling duo of Taskin Ahmed and Mustafizur Rahman provides a strong foundation, their batting unit desperately needs consistency. All eyes will be on players like Saif Hassan to replicate his form, and the team will be eager for a reliable top and middle-order effort to support the impressive control shown by spinner Rishad Hossain. A potential late entry for all-rounder Soumya Sarkar could be a crucial factor.

Afghanistan enters this series with a point to prove and a refreshed squad. Under the steady leadership of Rashid Khan, they've injected new, youthful energy with the inclusion of players like Wafiullah Tarakhil and Bashir Ahmad. They retain a powerful core, featuring the explosive batting of Rahmanullah Gurbaz and the spin wizardry of Rashid, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, and Noor Ahmad. Their spin-heavy attack, well-suited to the Sharjah pitch, will be their primary weapon as they aim to dominate their subcontinental rivals.

Welcome to the Sharjah Cricket Ground for the opening fixture of the three-match T20I series between Afghanistan and Bangladesh! After a disappointing Asia Cup campaign, both teams are looking to shake off the rust and stamp their authority early in this crucial series. With the T20 World Cup on the horizon, every game provides an invaluable opportunity to test combinations, find form, and build crucial momentum.
... MATCHDAY ...

The stage is set in Sharjah for a three-match T20I series between Afghanistan and Bangladesh, a contest that pits a star-studded, yet recently underperforming, Afghan side against a Bangladesh team looking to build on their Asia Cup Super Four berth. The deck at Sharjah is historically slow and low, often favouring the team batting first, where a 'slow and steady' approach is key to setting a competitive total. With both sides boasting quality spinners like Rashid Khan, Noor Ahmad, Nasum Ahmed, and Mahedi Hasan, the middle overs will be a crucial battleground, where turn and guile will likely supersede raw pace. Afghanistan, captained by the returning Rashid Khan, has plenty to prove, having lost three of their last four T20I encounters against the Tigers. The onus will be on the top order, particularly openers Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal, to lay a solid foundation on a difficult track. The experienced trio of Mohammad Nabi, Ibrahim Zadran, and Rashid himself provide a deep batting line-up, with all-rounder Azmatullah Omarzai also a vital cog in the middle. The bowlers, with Rashid leading the spin attack, will need their pacers to execute variations to find success on a surface that demands smart bowling. Bangladesh, led by Jaker Ali, enters the series with confidence from their Asia Cup win over Afghanistan, though their subsequent Super Four batting collapses against Pakistan and India remain a concern. While their bowling, featuring Mustafizur Rahman, Taskin Ahmed, and spinners Nasum and Rishad Hossain, has been impressive in recent outings, their top-order batting has been consistently underwhelming. Key batters like Towhid Hridoy, Soumya Sarkar, and Mahedi Hasan must deliver significant contributions, especially given the struggles of the opening pair. This series is a golden opportunity for both teams to fine-tune their T20 combination and iron out batting wrinkles before future assignments. For Afghanistan, the key is converting potential into performance, particularly with the bat. For Bangladesh, their formidable bowling attack gives them a fighting chance in any low-scoring scrap, but their top six must show resilience and intent to chase down or post a respectable total on this demanding ground. This surely promises to be a cracker.
